title: Red Lentil & Paneer Dal
seoTitle: Red Lentil & Paneer Dal | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: A creamy red lentil dal finished with seared paneer over basmati rice
subtitle: A creamy red lentil dal finished with seared paneer over basmati rice
description: Red lentils simmer down into a creamy dal with tomato, garlic, and warm spices, then get topped with seared paneer and a dollop of yogurt. It is a genuine vegetarian main, not a side dish, served over basmati rice.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse basmati rice and cook according to package directions. Fluff and hold covered.

steps.title: Build the dal base
steps.instruction: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot over medium. Cook onion 5–6 minutes until soft, then add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute more. Stir in garam masala, turmeric, and cumin and toast 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the lentils
steps.instruction: Add rinsed red lentils, crushed tomato, and vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils break down into a thick, creamy dal.

steps.title: Sear the paneer
steps.instruction: While the dal simmers, heat remaining oil in a skillet over medium-high. Sear paneer cubes 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Adjust seasoning and thickness
steps.instruction: Taste the dal and add salt or a splash of broth if it's too thick. It should be thick enough to hold on a spoon but still pourable.

steps.title: Serve
steps.instruction: Ladle dal over basmati rice, top with seared paneer, a dollop of yogurt, and cilantro if using.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover red lentil dal base — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool red lentil and paneer dal and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Rinse red lentils until the water runs mostly clear for the smoothest dal.
Rookie tip: Sear paneer close to service so it stays crisp instead of softening in the hot dal.
A spoon of ghee stirred in at the end (a classic tadka) adds real depth if the hall has it on hand.
tonightSpread: Main: Red lentil and paneer dal
Sides: Cucumber raita, simple green salad
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool red lentil and paneer dal in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Dal thickens in the fridge — loosen with a splash of water or broth when reheating.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is a one-pot, low-cleanup dinner that happens to be vegetarian, and the seared paneer on top makes it feel like a full entrée instead of a bowl of soup.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: the dal base holds and improves for up to 3 days. Storage: keep dal, paneer, and rice in separate containers up to 4 days. Reheating: reheat dal on the stove with a splash of water; sear paneer fresh or reheat gently so it doesn't turn rubbery.
substitutions: Use extra-firm tofu instead of paneer for a dairy-free-adaptable version.
Use canned lentils in a pinch, added in the last 10 minutes instead of simmering from dry.
Use brown rice instead of basmati for more fiber.
